children: Renewed inflationary pressure, particularly from higher oil and fuel prices has seen the South African Reserve Bank (Sarb) raise its key policy rate by 25 basis points, from 7% to 7.25%, and the prime lending rate to 10.75%.
The decision - taken by the Monetary Policy Committee, chaired by governor Lesetja Kganyago - was unanimous.
Since the MPC's July meeting this year, the conflict involving Iran and the wider Middle East has escalated, contributing to the higher oil prices and a more uncertain global economic outlook.
The latest decision aims to bring inflation back towards the Sarb's 3% target.
There is just one interest-rate announcement remaining this year.

title: ZAWYA: South African Reserve Bank hikes rates as oil, Middle East tensions bite
